newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond issuance seen strong this week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond issuance seen strong this week.

text.p: New issuance of corporate bonds in the U.S. is expected to continue at a brisk pace in the coming week, syndicate officials said.

Approximately $2.5 billion in new high-yield bonds are expected to be priced this week, including a $750 million two-tranche offering from Iridium LLC, a partnership building a global satellite communications service.
A favorable U.S. interest rate environment is also expected to attract the interest of investment-grade bond issuers, particularly those from outside the U.S.

Several sovereign issuers may tap the market this week. They include the Government of Canada with a $1.0 billion global offering of five-year bonds, the Republic of Lithuania with a $200 million 144A/eurobond offering of five-year notes, and Uruguay with a $300 million 30-year bond offering.

Among corporations issuing Yankee bonds this week, Chilean bank Banco Santiago may sell $200 million in 10-year Yankee debt via UBS Securities and Argentinean toll-road company Autopistas Del Sol SA may sell $380 million in debt in a two-part 144A deal via Citicorp Securities Inc.
Several domestic investment-grade deals that had been rumored for several weeks are expected to be priced shortly, now that most investors have returned from the holiday.
Tandy Corp may sell $300 million in 10-year debt via Bear Stearns Inc.
SAFECO Corp is also seen selling $750 million in 40-year capital securities, non-callable for 10 years, in a 144A transaction via Smith Barney Inc this week.
The company may also sell $200 million in senior notes.
New business also includes Greenpoint Financial Corp's $200 million offering of five-year notes (Baa2/BBB).
Goldman Sachs will be the lead-underwriter.
Returning to the junk bond primary market, market players said expectations were high for the new issuesr, despite a deterioration in conditions over the past several weeks.
While many junk bond investors still have sizable amounts of money to invest, experts noted the flow of new cash from mutual funds has slowed.
AMG Data Services reported that $183 million in net new cash flowed into junk bond mutual funds in the latest week, less than in many prior weeks, some of which saw inflows exceed $300 million.

In such an uncertain environment, market sources said they expect the large Iridium offering to be accompanied by warrants to sweeten the deal for investors. The deal will be lead-managed by Chase Securities Inc.

Other issuers expected to price this week include Ameristar Casinos Inc, with a $100 million 144a seven-year note offering via Bear Stearns, and Host Marriott Corp's HMH Properties Inc, with the sale of $600 million in 10-year 144a senior notes via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette.
